scenarios.title: Make a saved Ethernet profile follow supplied DHCP settings
scenarios.summary: Automatic profile selection and automatic IPv4 addressing are different choices. The worked profile remains eligible on enp1s0, but its IPv4 method obtains each test's address and router instead of storing one manual address.
scenarios.objective: At the next startup, configure Lab Ethernet on enp1s0 from each supplied DHCP address, prefix and router. Reach 172.16.5.10 through enp1s0 as the preferred default uplink. Preserve the current management connection and all protected management profile settings. Keep the supplied filenames and UUIDs; test every supplied case.
steps: Edit the saved virtual profile, test its next-startup behavior against all supplied leases and repair the specific failed requirement.
scenarios.explanation: Automatic profile selection and automatic IPv4 addressing are different choices. The worked profile remains eligible on enp1s0, but its IPv4 method obtains each test's address and router instead of storing one manual address.
hints: Compare autoconnect in [connection] with method in [ipv4]: they control different decisions.
This exercise's automatic IPv4 subset uses only the supplied lease. Remove old address1 and gateway properties rather than copying one test's values.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded in-process saved Ethernet settings and settled supplied DHCP outcomes. No real NetworkManager, host profiles, commands, network packets, lease server, renewal, timeouts, retries, profile fallback, DNS merging, extra static addresses with auto, gateway overrides or actual restart. Current selections are owned snapshots; re-reading does not reacquire them. Supplied route metrics are explicit inputs. Interface /31 and /32 remain special cases outside this conventional exercise.

scenarios.title: Keep a DHCP address without taking over the default route
scenarios.summary: never-default=true leaves the received address and local route in place while suppressing that adapter's received default. A larger route metric still leaves a default route present; disabling autoconnect loses the local connection as well.
scenarios.objective: At the next startup, keep Lab Ethernet on enp1s0 configured from each supplied DHCP address and prefix. Keep a usable path to the supplied local peer through enp1s0, with no default route on that adapter. Reach 172.16.5.10 through management on enp2s0 as the preferred default uplink. Preserve the current management connection and all protected management profile settings. Keep the supplied filenames and UUIDs; test every supplied case.
steps: Edit the saved virtual profile, test its next-startup behavior against all supplied leases and repair the specific failed requirement.
scenarios.explanation: never-default=true leaves the received address and local route in place while suppressing that adapter's received default. A larger route metric still leaves a default route present; disabling autoconnect loses the local connection as well.
hints: The task needs the DHCP address and local path, so disabling the connection removes too much.
Inspect the per-profile IPv4 default-route policy. Changing route-metric alone does not remove a default route.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded in-process saved Ethernet settings and settled supplied DHCP outcomes. No real NetworkManager, host profiles, commands, network packets, lease server, renewal, timeouts, retries, profile fallback, DNS merging, extra static addresses with auto, gateway overrides or actual restart. Current selections are owned snapshots; re-reading does not reacquire them. Supplied route metrics are explicit inputs. Interface /31 and /32 remain special cases outside this conventional exercise.
